plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — DESIGN-ONLY DOCUMENT (no experiment run, no results claimed)

Title: Blockwise Adam (BAdam) vs LoRA for finetuning Llama 3-70B on MathInstruct — zero-shot math benchmark comparison.

1. RATIONALE AND HYPOTHESIS
The question asks whether BAdam — a blockwise alternating optimizer that updates one transformer block (layer) at a time, keeping the rest frozen per stage — yields better zero-shot math performance than LoRA finetuning at 70B scale. The design is a controlled two-arm (plus control) comparison with budget-matched training and a single shared evaluation harness. Primary hypothesis H1: mean zero-shot exact-match accuracy of the BAdam-tuned model exceeds the LoRA-tuned model on GSM8K and MATH. Secondary questions: training memory/wall-clock per arm; whether either arm improves over the frozen base (anchoring headroom).

2. TREATMENT ARMS
- Arm A (LoRA): rank 64 LoRA on attention projections (q, k, v, o) of all 80 layers; alpha = 2×rank, dropout 0.05, BF16 adapter weights. Chosen setting — not from the material.
- Arm B (BAdam): standard block schedule — one transformer layer per stage, sequential sweep layer 1→80 per pass; per stage, AdamW updates only that block's parameters (4-bit quantized backbone frozen between stages), fixed LR with short warmup per stage. Number of block-sweep passes chosen so total token budget matches Arm A.
- Arm C (control, frozen base): Llama 3-70B evaluated zero-shot with no finetuning, identical prompt/extraction/scoring. Anchors the comparison.

3. CONTROLS HELD FIXED
- Base model: identical Llama 3-70B checkpoint snapshot and identical 4-bit quantization (NF4, double-quant) for all arms — quantization is a controlled shared factor, not a confound.
- Data: identical fixed MathInstruct subset (see budget), same preprocessing, same packing/truncation policy, same shuffled order (same seed), same chat/instruction template for both arms.
- Budget: identical training token budget and identical number of optimizer passes over the data (1 epoch over the same subset); BAdam's memory savings are NOT spent on extra data.
- Optimization: same global batch (in tokens), same LR cap, same gradient clipping. (Per-arm LR tuned by a small validation sweep is allowed and must be reported; if untuned, a single LR applies to both and is stated.)
- Decoding: greedy decoding (temperature 0), max new tokens 1024, same stop sequences, for all arms.
- Evaluation: one shared harness, one fixed zero-shot prompt template, one fixed answer-extraction rule and scoring function, applied identically to A, B, C.

4. DATASET AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
- Training data: MathInstruct (CoT-focused subset; PoT/code-execution items excluded or included as a documented choice — recommend CoT-only so chain-of-thought text generation matches zero-shot benchmark format; state the exclusion explicitly). Fixed subset of 100K examples, 1 epoch.
- Benchmarks (per researcher resolution): primary = GSM8K (test, 1,319 items) and MATH (test, 5,000 items; MATH-500 allowed as a documented cost-saving variant); optional tertiary = AQuA-RAT test, clearly marked optional.
- Zero-shot prompt: a single fixed instruction template with an answer-cue ("The final answer is ..."), identical across benchmarks within their format; no few-shot exemplars.
- Extraction/scoring: GSM8K — extract the last numeral (handling commas) after the answer cue; exact match to gold. MATH — extract final \boxed{} content, else the text after the cue; normalize LaTeX (strip spaces, canonical fractions) then string-equal match, noting MATH string-matching is an approximation of official equivalence grading. AQuA-RAT (optional) — extract the choice letter (A–E). The extraction function is a single frozen piece of code applied to all arms; 50-item manual audit of extraction failures reported as a sanity check.

5. TRAINING PROTOCOL (per arm)
- Sequence length 1,024; global batch ~64 sequences (gradient accumulation as needed).
- LR: 1e-4 (LoRA) / 1e-4 within-stage (BAdam) as starting points, cosine or per-stage constant decay, warmup 100 steps.
- Logging: loss vs tokens, grad norm, per-stage wall-clock; checkpoints at end only (design cost saving).

6. METRICS AND ANALYSIS PLAN
- Primary: zero-shot exact-match accuracy per benchmark per arm.
- Secondary: trainable-parameter count, optimizer-state memory, peak training memory, total wall-clock GPU-hours, loss curves.
- Statistics with a single seed: report per-benchmark accuracy with 95% bootstrap CIs over test items (e.g., 10,000 resamples) and paired item-level McNemar tests between A and B and between each arm and C on the identical item sets. Explicit caveat: item-level CIs reflect sampling uncertainty of test items, NOT training-seed variance; differences are therefore directional evidence unless the repeat-seed option is exercised.
- Repeat-seed option (if budget allows): rerun both training arms with 2 additional data-order/LR-tie-break seeds; then report mean ± range across seeds alongside item-level statistics.
- Effect sizes: absolute and relative accuracy differences per benchmark; per-item breakdowns by problem type/length (MATH subject and level tags if retained) as exploratory analyses.
- Fairness discussion (per resolution 2): report trainable params (~262M, ≈0.37% of model for Arm A — see §7 estimates) vs BAdam's per-stage footprint, and discuss that arms are budget-matched on data/tokens, not on parameter count; parameter-count differences are reported, not forced to zero.

7. MEMORY / COMPUTE FEASIBILITY ESTIMATES (design artifacts; approximations)
Reference setup: 8×80GB GPUs (e.g., 8×A100/H100-80G), 4-bit NF4 base.
- Arm A (QLoRA r=64 attention): base weights ≈ 35–40 GB; adapters ≈ 262M params ≈ 0.5 GB (BF16) + Adam states ≈ 2.1 GB (fp32 m,v) + grads ≈ 0.5 GB; activations dominate but fit with gradient checkpointing. Estimate: fits comfortably on 8×80GB with 1,024-token sequences; plausibly even on 1–2 GPUs with heavy accumulation. Wall-clock: ~30M tokens at modest throughput (~2–5k tok/s/GPU effective) ≈ roughly 1–4 hours of 8-GPU time per seed (order-of-magnitude).
- Arm B (BAdam): 4-bit base ≈ 35–40 GB; per stage, one block (~0.88B params) fp32 master weights ≈ 3.5 GB + Adam states ≈ 7 GB + that block's grads; activations similar to Arm A. Peak well under 80GB per GPU with sharding/QLoRA as in the BAdam literature. Wall-clock: similar token count but per-block optimizer passes add overhead; estimate 1.5–3× Arm A's wall-clock.
- Arm C: inference only, 1319+5000 (+AQuA) items at ≤1024 new tokens ≈ a few GPU-hours.
- Smaller-budget alternative (feasibility note): 70B QLoRA on a single 80GB GPU (long runtime) or substituting Llama 3-8B for pipeline bring-up; both change scope and must be reported as deviations, not silently substituted.
- These are order-of-magnitude planning numbers derived from parameter/memory arithmetic and public BAdam/QLoRA practice, not measured results.

8. ASSUMPTION REGISTER
Material-supported facts (from /workspace/task.json only): the research question; design-only status ("repositories and compute are not required"); nothing else. GSM8K/MATH/AQuA are NOT named in the material — benchmark selection is the researcher's resolution (1).
Chosen settings (design decisions, not facts from the material):
 (a) 4-bit NF4 base on 8×80GB reference hardware [researcher resolution 3];
 (b) LoRA rank 64, attention-only targets, alpha=2r, dropout 0.05 [resolution 2];
 (c) BAdam one-layer-per-stage sequential sweep, per-stage AdamW [resolution 2];
 (d) 100K-example CoT-focused MathInstruct subset, 1 epoch, ~30M tokens [resolution 5];
 (e) fixed zero-shot prompt + specified extraction rules [resolution 7];
 (f) greedy decoding, 1024 max new tokens;
 (g) single seed primary with repeat-seed option [resolution 6];
 (h) frozen-base control arm [resolution 4];
 (i) LR values and batch/sequence sizes are starting points subject to a reported validation sweep.
External-knowledge assumptions (not verifiable in the workspace): MathInstruct's schema/size (~262K examples) and its CoT/PoT composition; Llama 3-70B architecture numbers (80 layers, hidden 8192, GQA 8 KV heads, vocab 128256) used in the parameter arithmetic; GSM8K/MATH test-set sizes; BAdam memory characteristics. All are flagged as assumption-based estimates.

9. RISKS AND LIMITATIONS
- Single seed: training-run variance at 70B on ~30M tokens can be material; item-level statistics cannot capture it. Mitigation: repeat-seed option; conservative language on H1.
- Prompt/extraction sensitivity: zero-shot math accuracy is highly sensitive to the cue and extraction rule; frozen shared harness mitigates between-arm bias but not absolute-level bias; extraction audit included.
- MATH scoring approximation: string matching understates answers equivalent in value; documented as a limitation, applied equally to all arms.
- Budget parity vs optimization parity: BAdam's effective number of optimizer steps over each parameter differs from LoRA's; equal tokens/data is the chosen parity axis and is stated.
- Data subset bias: results may not transfer to full MathInstruct or to PoT-style data; subset documented and fixed.
- Quantization interaction: 4-bit base may interact differently with BAdam block updates than with frozen adapters; since quantization is shared, this affects absolute numbers more than the A-vs-B contrast, but it is a limitation.
- BAdam block-order sensitivity: sequential 1→80 sweep is one point in schedule space; negative result is schedule-conditional.
- Contamination/overfitting to GSM8K-style CoT in MathInstruct: possible; per-benchmark breakdown helps diagnose.
- Design-only: no experiment is run and no results are reported anywhere in this document; all numeric training/eval figures above are feasibility estimates, not outcomes.

END OF DESIGN DOCUMENT — awaiting researcher disposition; no execution authorized or performed.

Title: Blockwise Adam (BAdam) vs LoRA for finetuning Llama 3-70B on MathInstruct — zero-shot math benchmark comparison.

1. RATIONALE AND HYPOTHESIS
The question asks whether BAdam — a blockwise alternating optimizer that updates one transformer block (layer) at a time, keeping the rest frozen per stage — yields better zero-shot math performance than LoRA finetuning at 70B scale. The design is a controlled two-arm (plus control) comparison with budget-matched training and a single shared evaluation harness. Primary hypothesis H1: mean zero-shot exact-match accuracy of the BAdam-tuned model exceeds the LoRA-tuned model on GSM8K and MATH. Secondary questions: training memory/wall-clock per arm; whether either arm improves over the frozen base (anchoring headroom).

2. TREATMENT ARMS
- Arm A (LoRA): rank 64 LoRA on attention projections (q, k, v, o) of all 80 layers; alpha = 2×rank, dropout 0.05, BF16 adapter weights. Chosen setting — not from the material.
- Arm B (BAdam): standard block schedule — one transformer layer per stage, sequential sweep layer 1→80 per pass; per stage, AdamW updates only that block's parameters (4-bit quantized backbone frozen between stages), fixed LR with short warmup per stage. Number of block-sweep passes chosen so total token budget matches Arm A.
- Arm C (control, frozen base): Llama 3-70B evaluated zero-shot with no finetuning, identical prompt/extraction/scoring. Anchors the comparison.

3. CONTROLS HELD FIXED
- Base model: identical Llama 3-70B checkpoint snapshot and identical 4-bit quantization (NF4, double-quant) for all arms — quantization is a controlled shared factor, not a confound.
- Data: identical fixed MathInstruct subset (see budget), same preprocessing, same packing/truncation policy, same shuffled order (same seed), same chat/instruction template for both arms.
- Budget: identical training token budget and identical number of optimizer passes over the data (1 epoch over the same subset); BAdam's memory savings are NOT spent on extra data.
- Optimization: same global batch (in tokens), same LR cap, same gradient clipping. (Per-arm LR tuned by a small validation sweep is allowed and must be reported; if untuned, a single LR applies to both and is stated.)
- Decoding: greedy decoding (temperature 0), max new tokens 1024, same stop sequences, for all arms.
- Evaluation: one shared harness, one fixed zero-shot prompt template, one fixed answer-extraction rule and scoring function, applied identically to A, B, C.

4. DATASET AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
- Training data: MathInstruct (CoT-focused subset; PoT/code-execution items excluded or included as a documented choice — recommend CoT-only so chain-of-thought text generation matches zero-shot benchmark format; state the exclusion explicitly). Fixed subset of 100K examples, 1 epoch.
- Benchmarks (per researcher resolution): primary = GSM8K (test, 1,319 items) and MATH (test, 5,000 items; MATH-500 allowed as a documented cost-saving variant); optional tertiary = AQuA-RAT test, clearly marked optional.
- Zero-shot prompt: a single fixed instruction template with an answer-cue ("The final answer is ..."), identical across benchmarks within their format; no few-shot exemplars.
- Extraction/scoring: GSM8K — extract the last numeral (handling commas) after the answer cue; exact match to gold. MATH — extract final \boxed{} content, else the text after the cue; normalize LaTeX (strip spaces, canonical fractions) then string-equal match, noting MATH string-matching is an approximation of official equivalence grading. AQuA-RAT (optional) — extract the choice letter (A–E). The extraction function is a single frozen piece of code applied to all arms; 50-item manual audit of extraction failures reported as a sanity check.

5. TRAINING PROTOCOL (per arm)
- Sequence length 1,024; global batch ~64 sequences (gradient accumulation as needed).
- LR: 1e-4 (LoRA) / 1e-4 within-stage (BAdam) as starting points, cosine or per-stage constant decay, warmup 100 steps.
- Logging: loss vs tokens, grad norm, per-stage wall-clock; checkpoints at end only (design cost saving).

6. METRICS AND ANALYSIS PLAN
- Primary: zero-shot exact-match accuracy per benchmark per arm.
- Secondary: trainable-parameter count, optimizer-state memory, peak training memory, total wall-clock GPU-hours, loss curves.
- Statistics with a single seed: report per-benchmark accuracy with 95% bootstrap CIs over test items (e.g., 10,000 resamples) and paired item-level McNemar tests between A and B and between each arm and C on the identical item sets. Explicit caveat: item-level CIs reflect sampling uncertainty of test items, NOT training-seed variance; differences are therefore directional evidence unless the repeat-seed option is exercised.
- Repeat-seed option (if budget allows): rerun both training arms with 2 additional data-order/LR-tie-break seeds; then report mean ± range across seeds alongside item-level statistics.
- Effect sizes: absolute and relative accuracy differences per benchmark; per-item breakdowns by problem type/length (MATH subject and level tags if retained) as exploratory analyses.
- Fairness discussion (per resolution 2): report trainable params (~262M, ≈0.37% of model for Arm A — see §7 estimates) vs BAdam's per-stage footprint, and discuss that arms are budget-matched on data/tokens, not on parameter count; parameter-count differences are reported, not forced to zero.

7. MEMORY / COMPUTE FEASIBILITY ESTIMATES (design artifacts; approximations)
Reference setup: 8×80GB GPUs (e.g., 8×A100/H100-80G), 4-bit NF4 base.
- Arm A (QLoRA r=64 attention): base weights ≈ 35–40 GB; adapters ≈ 262M params ≈ 0.5 GB (BF16) + Adam states ≈ 2.1 GB (fp32 m,v) + grads ≈ 0.5 GB; activations dominate but fit with gradient checkpointing. Estimate: fits comfortably on 8×80GB with 1,024-token sequences; plausibly even on 1–2 GPUs with heavy accumulation. Wall-clock: ~30M tokens at modest throughput (~2–5k tok/s/GPU effective) ≈ roughly 1–4 hours of 8-GPU time per seed (order-of-magnitude).
- Arm B (BAdam): 4-bit base ≈ 35–40 GB; per stage, one block (~0.88B params) fp32 master weights ≈ 3.5 GB + Adam states ≈ 7 GB + that block's grads; activations similar to Arm A. - Arm C: inference only, 1319+5000 (+AQuA) items at ≤1024 new tokens ≈ a few GPU-hours.
- Smaller-budget alternative (feasibility note): 70B QLoRA on a single 80GB GPU (long runtime) or substituting Llama 3-8B for pipeline bring-up; both change scope and must be reported as deviations, not silently substituted.
- These are order-of-magnitude planning numbers derived from parameter/memory arithmetic and public BAdam/QLoRA practice, not measured results.

Chosen settings (design decisions, not facts from the material):
 (a) 4-bit NF4 base on 8×80GB reference hardware [researcher resolution 3];

External-knowledge assumptions (not verifiable in the workspace): MathInstruct's schema/size (~262K examples) and its CoT/PoT composition; Llama 3-70B architecture numbers (80 layers, hidden 8192, GQA 8 KV heads, vocab 128256) used in the parameter arithmetic; GSM8K/MATH test-set sizes; BAdam memory characteristics. All are flagged as assumption-based estimates.

9. RISKS AND LIMITATIONS
- Single seed: training-run variance at 70B on ~30M tokens can be material; item-level statistics cannot capture it. Mitigation: repeat-seed option; conservative language on H1.
- Prompt/extraction sensitivity: zero-shot math accuracy is highly sensitive to the cue and extraction rule; frozen shared harness mitigates between-arm bias but not absolute-level bias; extraction audit included.
- MATH scoring approximation: string matching understates answers equivalent in value; documented as a limitation, applied equally to all arms.
- Budget parity vs optimization parity: BAdam's effective number of optimizer steps over each parameter differs from LoRA's; equal tokens/data is the chosen parity axis and is stated.
- Data subset bias: results may not transfer to full MathInstruct or to PoT-style data; subset documented and fixed.
- Quantization interaction: 4-bit base may interact differently with BAdam block updates than with frozen adapters; since quantization is shared, this affects absolute numbers more than the A-vs-B contrast, but it is a limitation.
- BAdam block-order sensitivity: sequential 1→80 sweep is one point in schedule space; negative result is schedule-conditional.
- Contamination/overfitting to GSM8K-style CoT in MathInstruct: possible; per-benchmark breakdown helps diagnose.
- Design-only: no experiment is run and no results are reported anywhere in this document; all numeric training/eval figures above are feasibility estimates, not outcomes.
